Vol. 4, p. 594
1. “How can I sleep on the bed, when a general raid has not yet covered al-Shām? … It makes the old man forget his sons and shows the anklets of the virgin noblewoman.” By ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt. “How” is rhetorical, in the sense of denying sleep. “Lammā” has the sense of “lam,” except that it includes the continuation of the negation up to the time of speaking and the expectation of the event's occurring afterward. He likens the raid, that is, war, to something that encompasses and covers, by implicit metaphor, and the covering is the imaginative element; al-shaʿwāʾ means pervasive and spreading. Its making the old man forget his sons is a metonym for its intensity, and so is its uncovering of the anklets of the noblewoman; al-khidām means the anklet. The ʿaqīla of anything is its most honorable part; among women, the veiled one who is kept in her chamber. Al-ʿadhrāʾ is the one who is hard to attain and difficult to reach. There is iqwāʾ in it, which is a variation of the rhyme vowel between ḍamma and kasra. It is also transmitted with “al-ʿaqīla al-ʿadhrāʾ” in the nominative, as the subject of “shows,” and Ibn Jarīr made it evidence for the permissibility of dropping the tanwīn when a sukūn follows, though more often it is vowelled in that case; on this view the clause needs a link back to the described noun, which is “raid,” with the estimate: “and the noblewoman shows in it from an anklet.” 2. His phrase “as for the one who compared, due to his narrow range”: that is, whoever holds the doctrine of the Mushabbiha as established in kalām, as he will indicate later. (Editor) 3. Al-Ḥākim transmitted it through Salama ibn Kuhayl from Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ from Ibn Masʿūd, in the course of a long ḥadīth in which it is not explicitly raised to the Prophet. Al-Ṭabarī transmitted it in abridged form. 4. His phrase “as if there were skewers (safāfīd) in them”: the singular is sāfūd (with shadda on the fāʾ in the plural's root form), an iron rod on which meat is roasted, as al-Ṣiḥāḥ explains. (Editor)
1. (1) . كيف نومى على الفراش ولما
…. تشمل الشام غارة شعواء تذهل الشيخ عن بنيه وتبدى
…. عن خدام العقيلة العذراء لعبيد بن قيس الرقيات. وكيف استفهام إنكارى، بمعنى نفى النوم. ولما بمعنى لم، إلا أن فيها استمرار النفي إلى زمن التكلم وتوقيع الوقوع بعده. وشبه الغارة وهي الحرب بماله إحاطة وشمول على طريق المكنية، والشمول تخييل، والشعواء الغاشية المنتشرة، وإذهالها للشيخ عن بنيه: كناية عن اشتدادها، وكذلك كشفها عن خدام العقيلة، والخدام: الخلخال. وعقيلة كل شيء: أكرمه. ومن النساء المخدرة التي عقلت في خدرها. والعذراء: التي يتعذر نوالها ويشق وصالها. وفيه الاقواء، وهي اختلاف الروى بالضم والكسر. ويروى برفع العقيلة العذراء على أنه فاعل تبدى، وجعله ابن جرير شاهدا على جواز حذف التنوين إذا تلاه ساكن، وإن كان الكثير تحريكه حينئذ، وعلى هذا فتحتاج هذه الجملة إلى رابط يعود على المنعوت وهو غارة، والتقدير: وتبدى فيها العقيلة عن خلخال.
2. . «قوله وأما من شبه فلضيق عطنه» أى من قال بمذهب المشبهة على ما هو مقرر في علم الكلام، كما سيشير إليه بعد. (ع)
3. . أخرجه الحاكم من طريق سلمة بن كهيل عن أبى الزعراء عن ابن مسعود في أثناء حديث طويل ليس فيه تصريح برفعه. ورواه للطبري مختصرا.
4. . قوله «كأن فيها السفافيد» واحدها سفود بالتشديد، وهي حديدة يشوى بها اللحم. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 595
1. His phrase “while they were sound of back”: perhaps it should read “sound of back” by annexation (sālimū al-aṣlāb). (Editor) 2. His phrase “the meaning: it suffices Me as requiter”: the known usage is “it suffices you that I am a requiter” or “God suffices you as requiter.” (Editor)
1. (1) . قوله «وهم سالمون الأصلاب» لعله سالمو الأصلاب بالاضافة. (ع)
2. . قوله «والمراد حسبي مجازيا» الاستعمال المعروف: حسبك بى مجازيا. أو حسبك الله مجازيا. (ع)
13
Q 68:44–45 · Vol. 4, pp. 595–596

Verses 44 to 45

The verses as the commentary quotes them
“So leave Me with those who deny this statement; We will lead them on step by step from where they do not know (44), and I give them respite. Indeed My plan is firm (45)
فَذَرْنِي وَمَنْ يُكَذِّبُ بِهذَا الْحَدِيثِ سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَعْلَمُونَ (44) وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ (45)
Vol. 4, p. 595
.” One says “dharnī and him,” meaning “leave him entirely to me, and I will suffice you against him,” as if He said: it is enough to strike him that you entrust his matter to Me and leave Me alone with him, for I do what must be done to him and am able to do it. The meaning: it is sufficient for Me to be the one who requites [2] whoever denies the Qurʾān, so do not occupy your heart with his affair, and trust Me for the vengeance against him; this is consolation for the Messenger of God ﷺ and a threat to the deniers. Istadrajahu ilā kadhā means he brought him down to it step by step until he plunged him into it. God's leading the disobedient on step by step is that He gives them health and comfort, and they make God's provision a pretext and a ladder toward increase in disbelief and sin. “From where they do not know” means from the direction in which they do not sense that it is a leading on, which is His favoring them, because they think it a preferment of them and a favoring of them over the believers, when it is a cause of their destruction. “And I give them respite” means I grant them time, as in the words of the Almighty “We give them time only so that they may increase in sin.” Health, provision, and length of life are kindness and bounty from God that require gratitude and obedience from them, but by their own choice they make it a cause of disbelief; so when they were led by it step by step to destruction, the One who favored them was described as leading them on. It was said: how many are led on by kindness shown to them, how many are tried by praise of them, and how many are deceived by being protected from exposure. And
يقال: ذرني وإياه، يريدون كله إلىّ، فإنى أكفيكه، كأنه يقول: حسبك إيقاعا به أن تكل أمره إلىّ وتخلى بيني وبينه، فإنى عامل بما يجب أن يفعل به مطيق له، والمراد: حسبي مجازيا «2» لمن يكذب بالقرآن، فلا تشغل قلبك بشأنه وتوكل علىّ في الانتقام منه تسلية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وتهديدا للمكذبين. استدرجه إلى كذا: إذا استنزله إليه درجة فدرجة، حتى يورطه فيه. واستدراج الله العصاة أن يرزقهم الصحة والنعمة، فيجعلوا رزق الله ذريعة ومتسلقا إلى ازدياد الكفر والمعاصي مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَعْلَمُونَ أى: من الجهة التي لا يشعرون أنه استدراج وهو الإنعام عليهم، لأنهم يحسبونه إيثارا لهم وتفضيلا على المؤمنين، وهو سبب لهلاكهم وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ وأمهلهم، كقوله تعالى إِنَّما نُمْلِي لَهُمْ لِيَزْدادُوا إِثْماً والصحة والرزق والمدّ في العمر: إحسان من الله وإفضال يوجب عليهم الشكر والطاعة، ولكنهم يجعلونه سببا في الكفر باختيارهم، فلما تدرجوا به إلى الهلاك وصف المنعم بالاستدراج. وقيل: كم من مستدرج بالإحسان إليه، وكم من مفتون بالثناء عليه، وكم من مغرور بالستر عليه. وسمى
Vol. 4, p. 596
He called His kindness and enabling a “plan” (kayd), as He called it a “leading on,” because it has the form of a plan, being a cause of plunging into destruction; and He described it as firm because of the strength of the effect of His kindness in causing destruction.
إحسانه وتمكينه كيدا كما سماه استدراجا، لكونه في صورة الكيد حيث كان سببا للتورّط في الهلكة، ووصفه بالمتانة لقوّة أثر إحسانه في التسبب للهلاك.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 595
1. His phrase “while they were sound of back”: perhaps it should read “sound of back” by annexation (sālimū al-aṣlāb). (Editor) 2. His phrase “the meaning: it suffices Me as requiter”: the known usage is “it suffices you that I am a requiter” or “God suffices you as requiter.” (Editor)
1. (1) . قوله «وهم سالمون الأصلاب» لعله سالمو الأصلاب بالاضافة. (ع)
2. . قوله «والمراد حسبي مجازيا» الاستعمال المعروف: حسبك بى مجازيا. أو حسبك الله مجازيا. (ع)
14
Q 68:46–47 · Vol. 4, p. 596

Verses 46 to 47

The verses as the commentary quotes them
“Or do you ask them for a wage, so that they are burdened with debt? (46) Or is the unseen with them, so that they write it down? (47)
أَمْ تَسْئَلُهُمْ أَجْراً فَهُمْ مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ مُثْقَلُونَ (46) أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ (47)
Vol. 4, p. 596
” Al-maghram means a fine or debt, that is: you did not seek from them a wage for guidance and teaching, so that bearing fines on their wealth would weigh upon them and hold them back from faith. “Or is the unseen with them” means the Tablet, “so that they write” from it what they judge by.
المغرم: الغرامة، أى لم تطلب منهم على الهداية والتعليم أجرا، فيثقل عليهم حمل الغرامات في أموالهم، فيثبطهم ذلك عن الإيمان أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ أى اللوح فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ منه ما يحكمون به.
15
Q 68:48–50 · Vol. 4, p. 596

Verses 48 to 50

The verses as the commentary quotes them
“So be patient for the decree of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was choking with grief (48). Had not a favor from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast onto the bare shore while blameworthy (49). Then his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous (50)
فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلا تَكُنْ كَصاحِبِ الْحُوتِ إِذْ نادى وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ (48) لَوْلا أَنْ تَدارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَراءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ (49) فَاجْتَباهُ رَبُّهُ فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ (50)
Vol. 4, p. 596
.” “The decree of your Lord” is His giving them respite and delaying your victory over them. “And do not be like the companion of the fish” means Jonah ﷺ. “When he called out” in the belly of the fish “while he was choking with grief” (makẓūm) means filled with anger, from kaẓama al-siqāʾ when one fills the waterskin. The meaning is: let there not be found in you what was found in him of vexation and wrath, so that you would be tried with his trial. The masculine form of the verb is acceptable because the pronoun separates it from its subject in “reached him” (tadārakahu). Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd read tadārakathu. Al-Ḥasan read tadārakahu, that is, tatadārakuhu, to depict a past state, meaning: had it not been said of him “it will overtake him,” as one says “Zayd was about to stand, but so-and-so prevented him,” that is, it was said of him “he will stand.” The meaning is that standing was expected of him. “The favor of his Lord” is that He favored him with success in repentance and relented toward him. In the answer to “had not” he relied on the ḥāl, I mean the words “while he was blameworthy,” meaning that his state, when he was cast onto the bare shore, was the opposite of blameworthy, whereas without his repentance his state would have been blameworthy. It is reported that the verse was revealed at Uḥud when what happened to the Messenger of God ﷺ befell him, and he wished to call down a curse on those who fled. It was also said: when he wished to call down a curse on Thaqīf. It is also read raḥma min rabbihi. “Then his Lord chose him” means He gathered him to Himself and drew him near by relenting toward him, as He said, “Then his Lord chose him, and relented toward him and guided him.” “And made him one of the righteous” means one of the prophets. From Ibn ʿAbbās: God returned revelation to him and accepted his intercession for himself and his people.
لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وهو إمهالهم وتأخير نصرتك عليهم وَلا تَكُنْ كَصاحِبِ الْحُوتِ يعنى: يونس عليه السلام إِذْ نادى في بطن الحوت وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ مملوء غيظا، من كظم السقاء إذا ملأه، والمعنى: لا يوجد منك ما وجد منه من الضجر والمغاضبة، فتبتلى ببلائه. حسن تذكير الفعل لفصل الضمير في تداركه. وقرأ ابن عباس وابن مسعود: تداركته. وقرأ الحسن: تداركه، أى تتداركه على حكاية الحال الماضية، بمعنى: لولا أن كان يقال فيه تتداركه، كما يقال: كان زيد سيقوم فمنعه فلان، أى كان يقال فيه سيقوم. والمعنى: كان متوقعا منه القيام. ونعمة ربه: أن أنعم عليه بالتوفيق للتوبة وتاب عليه. وقد اعتمد في جواب «لولا» على الحال، أعنى قوله وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ يعنى أنّ حاله كانت على خلاف الذمّ حين نبذ بالعراء، ولولا توبته لكانت حاله على الذمّ. روى أنها نزلت بأحد حين حل برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما حل به، فأراد أن يدعو على الذين انهزموا. وقيل: حين أراد أن يدعو على ثقيف. وقرئ: رحمة من ربه فَاجْتَباهُ رَبُّهُ فجمعه إليه، وقربه بالتوبة عليه، كما قال: ثُمَّ اجْتَباهُ رَبُّهُ فَتابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدى فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ أى من الأنبياء. وعن ابن عباس: ردّ الله إليه الوحى وشفعه في نفسه وقومه.
16
Q 68:51–52 · Vol. 4, pp. 596–597

Verses 51 to 52

The verses as the commentary quotes them
“And indeed those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say: ‘Indeed he is mad’ (51). And it is nothing but a reminder for the worlds (52)
وَإِنْ يَكادُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصارِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُوا الذِّكْرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُ لَمَجْنُونٌ (51) وَما هُوَ إِلاَّ ذِكْرٌ لِلْعالَمِينَ (52)
Vol. 4, p. 596
.”
Vol. 4, p. 597
“In” (in) is the lightened form of the heavy “inna,” and the lām is its sign. It is read liyuzliqūnaka with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the yāʾ. Zalaqahu and azlaqahu have the same meaning; one also says zalaqa al-raʾs and azlaqahu for shaving the head. It is also read layuzhiqūnaka, from zahaqat nafsuhu and azhaqahā. The meaning is that, from the intensity of their staring and looking at you sidelong with eyes of enmity and hatred, they almost cause your foot to slip or destroy you, as one says “he looked at me a look that almost felled me” and “almost ate me,” meaning that if his look could fell or eat, he would. The poet said: “They lend one another, when they meet in a place, a look that makes the footholds slip.” [1] It was said that the evil eye was found among Banū Asad: one of them would go hungry for three days, and nothing would pass by him without his saying of it: “I have never seen the like of it today,” whereupon it would be struck. One of the evil-eyers was asked to say the like about the Messenger of God ﷺ and he said: “I have never seen a man like him today,” but God protected him. From al-Ḥasan: the remedy for being struck by the eye is to recite this verse. “When they heard the Reminder,” that is, the Qurʾān, they could not restrain themselves out of envy at the prophethood he had been given, “and they say: Indeed he is mad,” out of bewilderment about his affair and to drive people away from him, though they knew that he was the most sensible of them. The meaning is that they called him mad because of the Qurʾān. “And it is nothing but a reminder and an exhortation for the worlds,” so how could one who brought the like of it be called mad? From the Messenger of God ﷺ: “Whoever recites Sūrat al-Qalam, God will give him the reward of those whom God has made good in character.” [2]
إن مخففة من الثقيلة واللام علمها. وقرئ، ليزلقونك بضم الياء وفتحها. وزلقه وأزلقه بمعنى: ويقال: زلق الرأس وأزلقه: حلقه: وقرئ: ليزهقونك، من زهقت نفسه وأزهقها، يعنى: أنهم من شدّة تحديقهم ونظرهم إليك شزرا بعيون العداوة والبغضاء، يكادون يزلون قدمك أو يهلكونك، من قولهم: نظر إلىّ نظرا يكاد يصرعني، ويكاد يأكلنى، أى: لو أمكنه بنظره الصرع أو الأكل لفعله. قال: يتقارضون إذا التقوا في موطن … نظرا يزلّ مواطئ الأقدام «1» وقيل: كانت العين في بنى أسد، فكان الرجل منهم يتجوع ثلاثة أيام فلا يمر به شيء، فيقول فيه: لم أر كاليوم مثله إلا عانه، فأريد بعض العيانين على أن يقول في رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل ذلك، فقال: لم أر كاليوم رجلا فعصمه الله. وعن الحسن: دواء الإصابة بالعين أن تقرأ هذه الآية لَمَّا سَمِعُوا الذِّكْرَ أى القرآن لم يملكوا أنفسهم حسدا على ما أوتيت من النبوة وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُ لَمَجْنُونٌ حيرة في أمره وتنفيرا عنه، وإلا فقد علموا أنه أعقلهم. والمعنى: أنهم جننوه لأجل القرآن وَما هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ وموعظة لِلْعالَمِينَ فكيف يجنن من جاء بمثله. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة القلم أعطاه الله ثواب الذين حسن الله أخلاقهم» «2» .
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 597
1. He says: when they meet in an assembly (it is also transmitted “in a place”), yataqāraḍūn, that is, each lends the other something with his look at him, as if one gives his opponent a look and the other repays him with a look at him out of envy and rage. Making the footholds slip is a metonym for destruction, because one whose foot slips falls to the ground and may perish. That is: each looks at the other with the look of an envious, enraged person, and from this results the slipping of feet from their footholds; applying the slipping to the footholds is a rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī), because the foothold is the place of the foot, and it contains an exaggeration of the slipping of the foot. 2. Transmitted by al-Thaʿlabī, al-Wāḥidī, and Ibn Mardawayh from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
1. (1) . يقول: إذا للتقوا في مجلس- وروى موطن-: يتقارضون، أى: يقرض بعضهم بعضا بنظره إليه، كأن أحدهم يعطى خصمه النظر، والثاني يكافئه بنظره إليه حسدا وغيظا، وإزلال مواطئ الأقدام: كناية عن الإهلاك، لأن من زلت قدمه سقط على الأرض وربما هلك. أى: ينظر بعضهم بعضا نظر الحسود المغتاظ، فتسبب عن ذلك زلل الأقدام عن مواطئها، وإيقاع الازلال على مواضع الأقدام: مجاز عقلى، لأنه محله، وفيه مبالغة في زلل القدم.
2. . أخرجه الثعلبي والواحدي وابن مردويه عن أبى بن كعب.
